subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix path for exec approval stale writes, or sponsor a narrower allow-always-only repair for this issue?
rationale: The remaining fix changes exec approval security state, overlaps a dirty open security PR, and must choose a durable persistence boundary rather than another partial write-path patch.

options.title: Adopt or replace guarded writes
options.body: Refresh the shared lock/CAS direction on current main, close the unguarded-write and proof gaps, and use it to resolve this issue and the related stale-writeback class.

options.title: Sponsor narrow allow-always repair
options.body: Limit the fix to concurrent `allow-always` persistence if maintainers want to defer broader metadata and admin-writeback hardening.

options.title: Wait for the security PR track
options.body: Keep this issue open while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226 or a replacement decides the shared persistence primitive first.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace guarded writes
recommendation.body: Refresh the shared lock/CAS direction on current main, close the unguarded-write and proof gaps, and use it to resolve this issue and the related stale-writeback class.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and merged PR metadata make `vincentkoc` the strongest current-source routing candidate for the affected exec approval paths.
